title: Add a camera bar widget that turns every USB camera off

workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Open #13019 defines another omarchy.camera with the same two new widget files; they are competing implementations, not additive features
leads.consequence: #13019 also adds omarchy.camera with different UI (busy/idle/absent, no disable toggle) and its own camera-busy.sh plus tests. The heads diverge. Merging its diff onto this PR requires resolving add/add conflicts in Camera.qml and Camera.manifest.json (see merge13019/*.merged). Choosing this PR's files strands #13019's busy-state behavior and tests; choosing #13019's files removes the off switch added here. Resolve ownership or explicitly integrate both, rather than assume both can ship as separate widgets. GitHub reports #13019 MERGEABLE with quattro, which does not account for this PR's additions.
leads.triage: factual, verified (gh pr view 13019). Not published: outside this round's delta and already disclosed publicly in #13019's own description (which references #12972 and the offered split).

leads.summary: New camera udev rule missing from omarchy-settings backup=() alongside all existing package-owned udev rules
leads.consequence: The recipe installs etc/. into /etc, so this is a package-owned persistent camera policy. Unlike the other three listed udev rules, a local administrator edit to this file is not protected on the next package upgrade that changes the rule; pacman may replace it outright instead of retaining the local file and writing a .pacnew. This could unexpectedly reapply camera blocking or undo an administrator override. Add 'etc/udev/rules.d/70-omarchy-camera-disabled.rules' to backup=() in omarchy-settings (and dev recipe's matching list), or document that local policy must use an override file.
leads.triage: factual, verified against omacom-io/omarchy-pkgs PKGBUILD (blob 9fce62f8, lines 77-79 list only three udev rules). Not published: file unchanged this round, change belongs in omarchy-pkgs, and the rule is shipped policy rather than a user-edited config, so value is speculative.

leads.summary: Usage classifier reports non-USB and output-only /dev/video devices as use of an enabled USB webcam
leads.consequence: With any USB video-class interface present, apps opening a non-USB V4L2 MIPI/PCIe camera or an output-only virtual /dev/video node appear in apps and light the USB camera widget, because device identity/capture capability are never correlated with the USB interfaces counted by cameras_present. After disabling the USB interface, the status can still report inUse for that other device while the tooltip says Camera disabled; the other camera is not blocked by this toggle. Prefer matching holders/graph source to supported USB capture nodes, or describe the two scopes separately.
leads.triage: behavioural, pre-existing and unchanged since earlier reviews; manual documents USB-only scope. Not in delta; dropped for this follow-up (not confirmed by Opus).

leads.summary: The new test still passes when lasting_camera_users never detects any camera user; it also does not exercise the widget refresh
leads.consequence: The test asserts inUse is a boolean and apps is an array but never asserts their values while a camera is in use. In an isolated source-derived copy replacing the first sample with first="" (which makes every usage report false), all six test sections still pass under LC_ALL=C. Nor does the test assert the new onExited refresh path. Add two staged camera-user samples via injectable/stubbed /proc or pw-dump and assert a lasting holder is detected while a short enumerator is ignored; add a widget contract case for the refresh action if possible. This is a test-fidelity issue, not proof that production detection currently fails.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus test-validity note; Opus self-check C32 confirmed from pinned test source. Published as Optional test improvement.

leads.summary: The 300ms test intersects process names rather than holder identities, so two short opens from different same-named processes look lasting
leads.consequence: camera_users emits only /proc/PID/comm and drops the PID. If process A opens then closes /dev/video in the first scan, and a different process B with the same comm opens before the second scan, comm -12 matches their common name even though neither held the camera for 300ms. This is plausible for several browser/Electron subprocesses with the same comm or separate app instances enumerating concurrently after a hotplug. Keep PID (ideally PID plus process start time) through both samples and map to names only after intersecting; source alone proves the identity ambiguity, not its frequency on live hardware.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N2); corroboration. Published within trade-offs.

leads.summary: An enabled but invisible camera widget still scans every process and starts two watchers on machines with no USB camera
leads.consequence: The bar creates a widget instance for each screen when users enable it, even if present=false makes its slot width zero. Process running:true starts --watch unconditionally. Every 30-second timeout calls status and traverses all readable /proc/*/fd, while inotifywait and udevadm monitor stay alive. On a laptop with no supported USB camera, or after unplugging one, the icon is hidden but the scans and two waiters per display continue indefinitely. Skip the expensive process scan when no USB video interface is present; retain USB hotplug watch to wake when one appears.
leads.triage: behavioural, pre-existing and unchanged this round (new filter does not sleep on empty first sample). Dropped for this follow-up.

leads.summary: 300ms is not a guaranteed upper bound for Chromium's synchronous camera enumeration
leads.consequence: If a webcam's control/format queries or driver are slow enough to keep the V4L2 FD open longer than 300ms while merely enumerating, the bar still marks Chromium as inUse. The Chromium source establishes that GetDevicesInfo opens each /dev/video device and performs synchronous QUERYCAP/format/control ioctls before closing, but it contains no duration bound. The brief's measured 40-80ms and 100 short opens can hold on those machines without guaranteeing this for other devices. Settle with timestamped FD traces during enumeration across affected slow devices, or classify stream activity instead of elapsed open time.
leads.triage: hypothesis; overlaps Opus H-c. Covered by published trade-off note and 'Chromium itself was not run'. Not published separately.

limits: No assigned desktop slot or nested Quickshell session. Live QML rendering, user interaction, and kernel device unplug/replug were not exercised. This is not evidence that they fail.

Quickshell mirror, systemd, kernel, coreutils and Chromium source files fetched from current upstream without exact pinned Arch package revisions; version-sensitive behavior is not claimed from them alone.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up at `8543c417`, reassessing the [previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12972#issuecomment-5822442836) after the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12972#issuecomment-5824210011).

**Verified:** the three items from the previous review are resolved (the second one for the bar that was clicked), and the earlier findings (missing state directory, unrelated `/dev` opens, ancestor watch, redirection order, tmpfiles on upgrade) have not regressed. The new 300ms filter works as described. Two optional notes follow.

| Previous item | Status at `8543c417` |
|---|---|
| Watch test races its own stubs (optional test improvement) | **Resolved.** The `udevadm` stub logs before it records its PID, and `setpriv` arms the parent-death signal before exec, so waiting for the PID closes both races. A harness running the watcher's waiter with the test's stubs lost the monitor's log line 0 times in 3000 starts (17 with the old stub), and 0 against 81 in 1000 starts under CPU load. The full test passed 50/50, and 30/30 under load. It still fails every run with `wait` in place of `wait -n`, with the monitor started without `--pdeathsig`, with the back-off removed, or with a different udev filter. |
| Flag changes without a driver bind or unbind wait for the timeout | **Resolved for the bar that was clicked** (from Quickshell 0.3.1 source, not run in a live bar). `exited` fires when the toggle finishes, including a crash, and a refresh requested while one is still running is queued rather than dropped. The `toggleProc.running` guard keeps a second click from queuing a second toggle. See the multi-monitor note below. |
| Comments said a disabled camera "never gets a `/dev` node" | **Resolved.** Both comments now describe a disabled camera being unplugged, which has no node left to remove. The new `Camera.qml` comment matches the kernel source: writing `authorized` sends no uevent of its own. |

**Verified, 300ms filter:** measured with real file descriptors on a stand-in `/dev/video0` in a sandbox, a one-shot status that starts inside an 80ms open no longer reports the camera in use (0/20, against 20/20 at `ad2ae922`). In the watcher, a hold of 0.5s or longer shows up after 0.41 to 0.42s, against about 0.11s before. An app that opens the camera during the 0.3s wait is picked up on the next scan, because its event waits in the pipe. Chromium itself was not run.

The filter has side effects worth knowing about. None of them looks like a reason to change it unless the icon is meant as a strict privacy indicator:
- A real capture shorter than about 0.4s no longer lights the icon. Holds of 0.15 to 0.35s were shown before and are not now.
- Any update while an app holds the camera is about 0.3s later or more, including a second app joining or one of two releasing.
- The two samples are matched by process name, not PID. In a one-shot status (the refresh after a toggle), back-to-back 80ms opens by the same name that span more than about 0.3s still count as use: 4 in a row were reported 10/10, 3 in a row 0/10.

**Optional, other monitors:** the bar builds one Camera widget per monitor, each with its own watcher, and the new refresh reaches only the widget that was clicked. With no driver bound, the icon on other monitors can keep the old state for up to its 30s read timeout. [`BarWidget.broadcast()`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/8543c4176511be3eb05aa548f624f2756428f8b1/shell/Ui/BarWidget.qml#L25-L35) exists for this and is used by `SystemUpdate` and `Indicators`. For example, `onExited: root.broadcast("refresh")` with `function refresh() { refreshProc.running = true }`. Not tested. Toggles from the command line and manual flag edits can still wait up to the timeout in the no-driver case.

**Optional test improvement:** the test never stages a process holding a camera, and its status assertions check `inUse` and `apps` only by type, so the filter's second sample goes untested. A copy with the first sample forced empty, so that no app is ever reported, still passed every assertion. `camera_users` scans the real `/proc`, so an unprivileged test cannot stage a real holder, but `find` is called by bare name: a `find` stub on `PATH`, like the existing `inotifywait` and `udevadm` stubs, could report a lasting holder and a brief opener, with an assertion that only the first is reported. Not tested.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of `ad2ae922..8543c417` and of the Quickshell 0.3.1 `Process`, Linux USB and driver core, util-linux `setpriv` and coreutils `comm` sources involved. Isolated command-level runs: the PR's test (repeated, idle and under load, with mutants and the old test file), a race harness using the test's stubs, unit checks of the filter in three locales, and the real watcher with the real `inotifywait` and stand-in camera holders at both heads. No live bar or Quickshell session, udev daemon, USB hardware, root toggle, PipeWire or Chromium.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
